segments.text: Terrified of sweating in a meeting? The second you think 'don't sweat,' the faucet opens. The fear makes the symptom.
Frankl's fix is almost insultingly simple: walk in and try to sweat as hard as you possibly can.
The loop needs your resistance to survive. Chase the symptom on purpose, and it starves, often within a week.
Same with insomnia: try to stay awake, and sleep sneaks up. He called it paradoxical intention, the one trick of his modern therapy kept.
That's Man's Search for Meaning. Honest verdict on the channel.
